# M1-5b: nightly encrypted off-site backup to Turso + restore test

- Milestone: M1
- Branch / worktree: `t/M1-5b`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M1-5b`
- Depends on: M1-5a (merged, deployed)
- Touches (exclusive while running): new `backup/`; one snapshot method in `store/`; small wiring in `cmd/`, `config/`,
  `deploy/deploy.sh` (env keys only), `.env.example`
- Plan refs: architecture.md §6 (N4 backup; N3 secrets). Read only that. **Decision 2026-11-01 (Brendan):** the
  off-site target is Turso, holding only `age`-encrypted snapshot blobs, never plaintext and never a live replica.
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: yes (sup re-runs `./deploy/deploy.sh`)

## Goal
Every night `finbot serve` takes a consistent SQLite snapshot, encrypts it to the `age` recipient, and stores the
ciphertext in the Turso database `finbot-backup`, keeping the newest 14. A `finbot restore` command, run on Brendan's
Mac with the private key, gets the newest (or a chosen) backup back into a usable `.db` file.

## Config (already in the main checkout `.env`; never print values)
- `BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT`: the age public key (`age1…`). Not secret.
- `BACKUP_TURSO_URL`: `libsql://finbot-backup-deasa…`.
- `BACKUP_TURSO_TOKEN`: secret.
- Private key: `~/.config/finbot/backup-age.key` on the Mac only. It **must never** be copied to hoid or into a worktree.
  `restore` takes its path as a flag.
- New optional `BACKUP_AT` (local time of day, default `03:17`) and `BACKUP_KEEP` (default 14). Backups are disabled,
  with a startup log line saying so, when any of the three required vars is empty.

## Scope
1. **Snapshot (`store/`):** `DB.Snapshot(ctx, path)` using `VACUUM INTO` (consistent under WAL; safe while sync runs).
2. **`backup/`:**
   - encrypt the snapshot with `filippo.io/age` (pure Go; no age CLI in the image);
   - talk to Turso over its HTTP API (Hrana `/v2/pipeline`) with `net/http`, or a pure-Go libsql client (CGO stays off);
   - table `backups(id TEXT PK, created_at TEXT, size INTEGER, sha256 TEXT, chunk INTEGER, data BLOB)`. Split the
     ciphertext into chunks (pick a size safely under Turso's per-request limit, find out and record that limit in
     your Result). Write all chunks of one backup in one transaction, so a backup is all or nothing;
   - prune to `BACKUP_KEEP` newest only after a successful write;
   - temp files go in `/tmp` (tmpfs in the container) and are deleted whether the run succeeds or fails;
   - errors and logs never contain the token or URL credentials (reuse `cmd`'s scrub, or scrub in `backup/`).
3. **Commands (`cmd/`):**
   - `finbot backup`: one backup now, then print id, size, chunk count;
   - `finbot backup --list`: id, time, size (no data);
   - `finbot restore --key <path> [--id <id>] --out <path>`: download, check sha256, decrypt, write the `.db`, then run
     `PRAGMA integrity_check` on it and print row counts for the main mirror tables;
   - `serve` runs the backup daily at `BACKUP_AT` on the existing scheduler (the same no-overlap rule as sync); one log
     line per run (ok with size, or a redacted error).
4. **Deploy:** `deploy.sh` adds `BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT`, `BACKUP_TURSO_URL` and `BACKUP_TURSO_TOKEN` (and the two
   optional keys if present) to the generated `finbot.env`, with the same stdin/0600 handling. Nothing else changes.

## Out of scope
- Slack status / alerts (M1-5c), kids-ledger backups, a scheduled restore test on hoid (the private key isn't there).
- Any change to sync, ynab, or the mirror schema.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Unit tests: chunking round-trip (sizes 0, 1 chunk, exactly N chunks, N+1); sha mismatch → restore fails; prune
      keeps newest K; disabled when a required var is empty; scrub removes the token from errors.
- [ ] Round-trip against a fake Turso (`httptest`) end to end: backup → list → restore → identical DB content.
- [ ] **Live against `finbot-backup`** from the worktree with a temp DB that has had one real `finbot sync` (read-only
      YNAB): `finbot backup` succeeds; `backup --list` shows it; `restore --key ~/.config/finbot/backup-age.key --out
      <tmp>` passes integrity_check and its row counts equal the source DB's. Run twice and confirm both are listed;
      then set `BACKUP_KEEP=1`, run again, and confirm pruning. Delete the temp files afterwards. Secret grep of all
      output before printing: token 0, plan id 0.
- [ ] Inspect a stored blob with `turso db shell finbot-backup "select id, length(data) from backups limit 3"`:
      only ciphertext sizes; confirm the first chunk starts with the age header (`age-encryption.org/v1`), not
      `SQLite format 3`.
- [ ] `docker build .` passes; `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green.
